cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: An authentication scheme is how a client proves its identity to a server on a request: what credential it presents and how the server checks it. Credentials can be a shared secret like an API key or password, a token issued earlier, or a certificate.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Browser users: session cookies or OAuth 2.0 with OpenID Connect. APIs: bearer tokens such as short-lived JWTs. Simple machine access: API keys. High-security service-to-service: mTLS or HMAC signing. Trade-offs are statefulness, scalability and how easily a credential can be revoked. Basic auth is only Base64, so it needs HTTPS.

questions.q: What is a downside of JWTs?
questions.a: They are stateless, so they are hard to revoke before they expire.
